question: What labels should each conversation carry?

options.name: Today's seven labels
options.description: warming, readyToAsk, askedWaiting, friend, client, cold, skip, as one field.

options.name: Two fields: who and where
options.description: who: lead, client, partner, friend, community, bot (owner-editable list); where, only for leads and clients: new, warming, need found, offered, call booked, won, lost, gone quiet (owner-editable list).

options.name: Two fields plus next move
options.description: B, plus the next move the plays should make (answer, follow up, ask, book the call, stop), learnt later from outcomes.

options.name: Free-text summary only
options.description: No fixed labels; a model writes a short summary of each conversation.

criteria.question: How well does it keep bots, friends and partners out of sales stages and say where a lead really is?
How directly can log's plays choose their move from it?
How easy is it for a small local model to learn from a few examples?
How easy is it for the owner to read and correct?
How small is the change to src/inbox/label and its readers?

question: What should label each conversation, every time a message lands?

options.name: Today's counting rules
options.description: autoLabel: back-and-forth counts, days quiet, an unanswered ask.

options.name: SubQ on every message
options.description: Send the chat to SubQ on each new message and use its answer.

options.name: Zero-shot local classifier
options.description: A small zero-shot classifier (GLiClass-style) on the CPU, no training, labels from their names.

options.name: Distilled local labeller
options.description: The owner labels 30-40 chats picked by active learning; SubQ labels all chats once with candidate labels when unsure; a SetFit labeller on the shipped MiniLM learns from his labels plus the confident ones and runs on every message on the CPU; unsure chats go back to SubQ or the owner.

options.name: Fine-tuned small generative model
options.description: Fine-tune a 0.5-2B generative model to output the labels.

criteria.question: How often will it agree with the owner on who and where?
How fast per new message on this laptop's CPU?
How little does it cost to run on every message?
How little of the owner's messages leaves the machine on each message?
How well does it keep up as stages and people change?
How small is the build for log (Bun/TypeScript, Python, ONNX models already pinned)?

question: How should log find that two accounts are the same person?

options.name: Today's Fellegi-Sunter, three comparisons
options.description: Shared posts, handle, display name; the owner says yes.

options.name: More comparisons in the same model
options.description: Keep Fellegi-Sunter and the owner's yes; add comparisons: writing style (character n-grams and his-style embedding of their messages), activity hours, topics they discuss with the owner, in-chat mentions of another handle ('my insta is ...'), and shared group chats; hard vetoes (different known real names, both active in the same chat as two people); a merge across existing people is re-checked.

options.name: LLM decides each pair
options.description: SubQ reads both identities' profiles and messages and says same or different, with multi-step reasoning.

options.name: B, then SubQ on the review band
options.description: B scores every pair; only pairs in the review band go to SubQ's multi-step check; the owner still says yes.

criteria.question: How many real same-person pairs (like a friend's Discord, X and Instagram with different handles) will it find?
How safe is it from merging two different people?
Can the owner see why a pair was suggested?
How cheap to run over all pairs?
How small is the change to src/people?

question: Where does the ground truth come from?

options.name: Only the owner's hand labels
options.description: The owner labels everything he cares about by hand.

options.name: Only SubQ's labels
options.description: SubQ labels every chat; no owner labels.

options.name: Owner labels chosen by active learning, plus confident SubQ labels
options.description: The owner labels 30-40 chats picked as the most informative, in a form in the chat; SubQ labels the rest with candidates when unsure; only confident SubQ labels train the labeller; disagreements go to the owner; outcomes (deals won, clients) are recorded as they happen.

criteria.question: How trustworthy are the labels a model learns from?
How little of the owner's time does it take?
How stable is a model trained on it across runs?
